certainty_reasoning: Married, but on the weakest kind of web sourcing: an uncited Wikipedia sentence, with Wikidata giving a different year and no reference either.
date_label: M. 1902 (Wikidata says 1901); ended by his death, 3 May 1904
summary: Widowed since 1894, Mary Robinson married the microbiologist Emile Duclaux in 1902, having moved among the scientific community of France. He died two years later. She did not marry again, kept his name, was hidden with her sister at Aurillac when war came in 1939, and died there in 1944 at eighty-six.

sources.quote: Robinson mingled with the scientific community of France as well, and in 1902 she married Emile Duclaux, a student of the biologist and chemist Louis Pasteur.
sources.context: Wikipedia, 'Agnes Mary Frances Duclaux', section 'Life'. Wikidata Q517162 gives 1901 for the same marriage, also without a reference.
sources.supports: The second marriage, its year and the husband's identity.
